content.title: About
content.content: The frozen coffee drink is a ready‑to‑serve beverage made from cold coffee, sugar and dairy components, frozen to a soft‑serve ice‑cream consistency. It combines the aroma of freshly brewed coffee with a refreshing chill, perfect for hot days.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first frozen coffee drink appeared in Japan in the 1990s under the brand “Frappuccino”.
Stabilizers are often added to prevent ice crystal formation and keep a creamy texture.
It can be made at home using coffee syrup, milk and liquid nitrogen.
There are many flavor variations: vanilla, caramel, mint, chocolate, and spiced.

items.title: Source of caffeine
items.content: Caffeine boosts alertness and may improve concentration.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Coffee is rich in polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Energy support
items.content: Sugar and dairy proteins provide a quick energy boost.

items.title: Mood enhancement
items.content: Caffeine stimulates dopamine production, contributing to a better mood.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: High caffeine intake can cause anxiety, insomnia, and rapid heartbeat.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: High sugar levels may contribute to weight gain and increase diabetes risk.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Dairy ingredients can cause discomfort for people who are lactose intolerant.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the frozen coffee drink in a glass with a straw; you can top it with whipped cream, dust with cocoa powder, or add a scoop of ice cream for extra richness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in the freezer at –18 °C. Over time ice crystals may form; let the drink sit at room temperature for 2–3 minutes before serving to soften.
